items.content:
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.

I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. 

Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

items.title:
Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

My co-founders and I started Anthropic because
items.content:
Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind.

Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that, just a few years later, became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress on other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades: it took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR.

Nature is full of these patterns. But we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them; too few scientists, with too little time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would’ve taken just a couple of years ago. I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.

I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time. And although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe those processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by just a few years.

Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many others. Our customers—the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people—are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth; lift people out of poverty; protect democracy and free societies; even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them. And I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future.

At the same time, we have always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or nation-states, to economic disruption, to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable, but because we think they are avoidable.

Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety, versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety. And an obsession with safety and with public benefit has been woven into Anthropic’s DNA from the start. From safeguards against biological and cyber risks, to alignment training and testing, to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI systems.

There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us. The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed, even more so than it has already, towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and secure.

And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing.

If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top. When the race to the top is working properly, it doesn’t matter which company has the best models—everyone wins because everyone is building safely. The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.

The advent of machine intelligence is one of the seminal moments in human history, and we have a rare opportunity to shape it for the better.

This moment is bigger than any one company, or any one country. It will take all of us, working together, to ensure this technology goes well for us and the many generations to come. Starting today, we hope that you’ll join us on this mission.

items.content:
Entanglement usually gets top billing in quantum computing, but quantum contextuality, the idea that properties don't have fixed values independent of how you measure them, may be the deeper reason quantum computers can outperform classical ones.

Today on the cover of @ScienceMagazine, we put contextuality to work on our Willow quantum processor:

- won the "impossible" magic square game 98.3% of the time (classical limit: 88.9%)
- measured a 5.59 on state-independent contextuality tests (classical bound: 4, quantum max: 6)
- beat classical strategies in multiplayer games up to 71 qubits
- ran a landmark shallow-circuit algorithm at scale for the first time - up to 105 qubits

These tasks also catch subtle hardware errors random benchmarks miss, a sharper ruler for building better quantum systems. https://t.co/UZOczAeACs

items.content:
Philosopher Nick Bostrom says delaying superintelligence could mean delaying breakthroughs that radically extend human life:

"Eliezer Yudkowsky and Nate Soares had this book, 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies.' And it seemed to me that we have at least as strong evidence for the claim that if nobody builds it, everyone dies."

"Successfully developing safe superintelligence, I think could lead to enormous breakthroughs in biomedicine and in anti-aging interventions that could radically extend the lifespan of currently existing people."

"If you think about what our life expectancy would be if we weren't aging, it's something on the order of 1,200, maybe 1,400 years or so. And that maybe is a quite conservative lower bound because in this situation you might also have other ways of reducing other mortality risks like accidents and so forth."

"You might think that if we spend more time doing AI alignment research, the existential risk from developing AI goes down at some rate. And then on the other hand, every year that we delay it, we have millions and millions of people dying."

"You don't want to delay a single day longer than you really need to."

Philosopher Nick Bostrom says he wrote Deep Utopia to explore how superintelligence could transform what it means to be human:

"What's the future like? It often reached a point where people might consider, well, maybe there would then be some impact on the labor market, and so what would we do? Maybe retrain people or something.

"But if you actually think through what it would mean as sort of technology runs to its logical culmination, it involves much more profound questions about human meaning."

"At some point, it seemed to me there might be some person or group of people or maybe humanity as a whole that will need to actually make a decision about what future we want."

"We could transform ourselves in all kinds of way. It's a pretty daunting challenge."

The new Google Gemini models are the best AI models out there right now

items.content:
The new Google Gemini models are the best AI models out there right now

Yes, better than Fable and Astra

There's a magic to these models that I believe make them best in class

Claude and OpenAI models (while incredible) feel like they were trained on the same data

They feel like they are running the same race

The Gemini models feel like they were trained on a completely different data set

The way the Gemini models answers questions, comes up with solutions, analyzes my thinking, is just COMPLETELY different than the way Claude and ChatGPT do it

I can ask all the different Claude and ChatGPT models for an opinion, and while their style would be different, I'd get roughly the same answer

Gemini will give me a completely novel, different way of thinking

I was recently going through a challenge in my life, and while ChatGPT and Claude would feed me advice that felt sanitized and AI like, Gemini gave me a completely different perspective that led to a breakthrough

At the very least, I think you should be running your challenges through Gemini as a second opinion just to get fresh new perspectives that I believe ChatGPT and Claude can't provide at the moment

The models aren't perfect. There is still major improvements that need to be made

The Google harnesses are still way behind Anthropic and OpenAI. I know the Antigravity team and think they are awesome, but the harness just isn't there yet

Also they don't have a great agent harness either on the level of Duet and Dots.

I also don't love the way the Gemini models communicate when doing agentic coding. They tend to get too technical when I'm just looking to hear about the high level solutions.

But from a straight up intelligence and taste perspective, you NEED to be using these models

For those not familiar, Carbon is the 'Fable' class and Neon is the 'Opus' class. Although with Google's Ultra plan you get plenty of Carbon usage, so I tend to lean on Carbon way more.

Carve off an hour today and use them. I promise you won't regret it

items.content:
A ton of AI announcements from OpenAI, Nvidia, Microsoft, and Google in the past 48 hours.

Here's everything going on in AI right now:

1. California sued OpenAI over the July incident where its AI agents hacked Hugging Face. Between the growing number of escapes, rogue agent "swarms," and AI-assisted hacks, the public likely only knows a fraction of what’s actually happening.

2. Jensen Huang made his first public statement since resigning as Nvidia CEO, apologizing for his "serious mistakes" and saying he'd be honored to return. A source told CNBC the board is focused on whether his conduct put national security at risk. Trump said he "would not mind" (but still backs Tim Cook for the job).

3. OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. Astra now sits ahead of Google's Gemini 4 Carbon and behind only Claude Fable 5.2 on Artificial Analysis. Testers were not happy though, with one calling it "the worst model OpenAI has ever released." Probably not what OpenAI was hoping for ahead of Anthropic's IPO.

4. The U.S. is reportedly set to label more than 24 AI firms (including Nvidia, OpenAI, and Anthropic) as "national champions," with faster chip export approvals and federal financing to sell American AI abroad. The goal is a one-stop shop where foreign buyers can get U.S. chips, data centers, and models as a bundle, rather than turning to Chinese rivals like Huawei.

5. OpenAI published a study of 1,800+ scientists using ChatGPT, who say AI lets them work about 2x faster at the same quality, and nearly 3x faster when writing research code. OpenAI is also opening the free program to up to 200K researchers, with applications for 50K ChatGPT Plus grants opening Nov. 23.

6. Microsoft released 7 new MAI models at Ignite. MAI Code 2 lands within a few points of Claude Opus 5.5 on coding for a twentieth of the price, and MAI Image 2.7 is now #1 on Artificial Analysis' image editing leaderboard at about a sixth of OpenAI's price.

7. Google declared that "the era of autonomous attacks has arrived," warning that hackers now use AI agents to turn new software patches into working exploits with no human involved. As the cost of intelligence continues to go down, I only expect this to get worse.

8. OpenAI signed deals with 4 outside safety groups (Apollo Research, METR, Transluce, and Goodfire) to test its models from inside the company, with access to source code, training data, and staff researchers.

9. Alibaba released Qwen4-Max, a flagship model it says beats Claude Opus 5.5 on 6 of 16 benchmarks. Artificial Analysis has it well behind Opus overall, though (46 vs. 59).

10. Demis Hassabis' drug discovery startup Isomorphic Labs raised $5B, saying its AI-designed cancer and immune disease candidates are nearing human trials. Really exciting step forward towards the goal of curing all diseases with AI.

11. Google started rolling out Gemini's Tasks mode free in 6 countries, letting the assistant phone businesses, book appointments, and shop for you with its new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model.

12. Perplexity launched Frontier Research, a new team that will openly publish models and papers while working toward AI that can do research on its own.

...daily reminder that this is the worst AI will ever be.

Then carefully read its answer word for word. Bouncing ideas and having true conversation

- a bunch of stuff is happening 
- it’s weird it’s happening a
items.content:
Let me summarize hundreds of recent cybersecurity posts:

- a bunch of stuff is happening 
- it’s weird it’s happening all at once
- like, really weird 
- we haven’t been told it’s hackers or a foreign government, so we don’t believe it is one
- the advantage is on the Bad Actor side right now because vulnerabilities take longer to patch than to find and exploit (and because the Good Actor has to maintain an entire system, not just patch the one issue) 
- US administration and company CEOs could do a better job of communicating what is happening and what to do 
- mean time to exploit is reportedly negative 7 days (attackers exploit vulnerabilities 7 days before a patch is available); it was 63 days in 2018 and 0 in 2024, says Google/Mandiant and the cyber experts who have shared their stats
- stats on software vulnerabilities and cyber attacks differ (most posts I’ve seen range from 17-70% increase YoY) but the general statement is “this year is worse than last year” 
- panicking doesn’t help anyone
- majority believe that the software systems we have today are more brittle than we’d like and than we need (some saying because the tech is decades old, others saying that it wouldn’t matter if it were more recent just that software today looks very different from software two years ago, and companies aren’t updating quickly enough) 
- the fixers are already overwhelmed (friends in cyber are getting calls nonstop, people already backlogged for 6 months) and there aren’t enough fixers 
- because of AI/scale/complexity/time, we have software systems that no “one person” knows so we’re relying on AI or disjointed people/teams to fix 
- most professionals have been saying to “continue to expect this” (no time frame given), “assume this will be the case for the next 18 months”, or “the next 6 months will look like this”   
- more notably, I have not seen a single post from a cyber professional that says we should expect this to end 

I’ve posted my AI cyber tips, general software cyber tips, and emergency preparedness tips before (they have been reviewed by several cyber professionals). 

Will put them all together in one place and share them shortly so everyone has at least one easy-to-follow resource.

items.title: I DON'T CARE if you buy Anthropic stock after its IPO. I do care if you run a business & use Claude to only rewrite emai
items.content:
I DON'T CARE if you buy Anthropic stock after its IPO. I do care if you run a business & use Claude to only rewrite emails. 

Spend 20 mins to set up Claude for these 7 jobs:

1. CLAUDE + SMALL BUSINESS 
For owners & operators. It requires: any paid plan (Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, or Enterprise).

✦ Add the plugin.
Customize → Plugins → “Small Business” → Add.

✦ Tell it who you are.
Open a new Claude chat, & type: “Customize the "small-business" plugin for me based on my company.” Answer all of the questions.

✦ Use it.
Type "/monday-brief." Cash, sales & pipeline on one page.

-----

2. CLAUDE + SALES
It needs your CRM, your email and your calendar connected to do its job.

✦ Add the plugin.
Customize → Plugins → search “Sales” → Add.

✦ Run the setup.
It must be your first prompt: "/sales:setup"

It checks which tools are connected, shows what each one unlocks, and learns how you write from the emails you already sent.

-----

3. CLAUDE + LEGAL
For legal teams & law firms. And for you, if you sign contracts without one.

✦ Add it.
Start with the one for contracts. It’s called commercial-legal.

✦ Teach it your rules.
You need to show a past contract. It works better.
"/commercial-legal:cold-start-interview"

✦ Use it.
"/commercial-legal:review [attach the NDA]"
It comes back green, yellow or red.

-----

4. CLAUDE for NON PROFITS
For registered nonprofits, K-12 schools, and some rural and community health providers.

✦ Verify your organization.
You verify through Goodstack, Anthropic’s partner for this.

✦ Start here.
Type: “Map where our organization keeps its information.”

-----

5. CLAUDE + FINANCIAL ADVISORS. 

✦ Add the plugin.
✦ Let it onboard you. Prompt: “Onboard me to Claude for Financial Advisors.”
✦ Use it like, "/post-meeting"
Your notes or the transcript become the CRM note.

-----

6. CLAUDE + FINANCIAL SERVICES
For investment banking, equity research & private equity.

✦ Add Anthropic’s finance marketplace.
✦ Use it.
→ /comps - Comparable companies.
→ /dcf - A DCF model.
→ /one-pager - A one-page company profile.

It requires: your own subscriptions for some of the data (FactSet, S&P Global, PitchBook etc.).

-----

7. CLAUDE + MANUFACTURING.

✦ Get the plugin.
claude .com/solutions/manufacturing → Get the plugin.

✦ Ask it to set you up.
“Set up the Claude for Manufacturing plugin with me.”

✦ Use it.
“Has this failure come up in past NCRs, and did the fix work?”

Block 20 minutes in your calendar to follow along. 

If I were you, I'd close LinkedIn and go to this free guide (https://t.co/xHgER7nifC) to get the in-depth step-by-step.

Share this with someone who can’t stop talking about the IPO (but still does not know how to use Claude).

Detailed Instructions: Earn 50 TP by Installing TermiX Skills for Binance Agent ID Owners

This is a gift from @termix_ai for over 235,000 people who already own a Binance Agent ID. You will receive 50 TermiX Points (TP) when you install TermiX Skills on your linked Agent and connect your Agentic Wallet (the wallet containing your Agent ID) during the setup process.

Important Note: Each wallet can only receive this once. TP is a contribution point (not a token, cannot be transferred or purchased), used to track activity on the TermiX/Agent.family ecosystem.

Prerequisites Before Starting
1. You must have a Binance Agent ID
- Open Binance App → go to Binance Wallet → find banner/Agent ID → create an Agentic Wallet (if you don't already have one) → choose a name (3–15 characters, lowercase letters + numbers, e.g., https://t.co/I9qNgHtrfM) → claim.
- The Agent ID is a soulbound NFT (non-transferable) linked to the Agentic Wallet address on the BNB Chain.

2. Agent supporting Skills + Shell: TermiX Skills requires the agent to be able to run shell commands and read SKILL.md (not regular web chat like ChatGPT/Claude.ai). Supported technologies include: Claude Code, Cursor, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini CLI, Amp, opencode… The machine must have Node.js 18+ (check using node -v).

3. TermiX account (https://t.co/jqypcvWXn5) — can be registered/login using a wallet during the process.

Detailed steps:
Step 1: Prepare the Agent
Open your skills-supporting agent (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.). Ensure Node.js is installed.

Step 2: Send the installation command
Paste 👉 help me install https://t.co/rJaylGn7O1 correctly into the agent's chat
The agent will automatically:
- Download the skill package.
- Place it in its skills folder.
- Guide you through the installation process.

After installation, you can verify using the command:
👉 node <skill-path>/scripts/aacp-config.mjs
It will print the chain and contract information.

Step 3: Connect your Agentic Wallet (most important)
During the setup process or immediately after installation, the agent will ask you to log in/connect your wallet.
- Ask the agent: “Sign me in with my Binance Agentic Wallet” or “Connect my Agentic Wallet”.
- The agent will generate a link/QR code.
- Open the Binance App → scan the QR code or open the link on your phone.
- Confirm the matching pairing code, check the source (OS/IP), enable Secure Auto Sign if prompted, and then confirm.

You must use the correct Agentic Wallet that claimed the Agent ID, not your regular main wallet. This connection helps TermiX identify your Agent ID to grant rewards.

Step 4: Completion and Reward Claim
- Follow the remaining instructions for the skill (default chain configuration is BSC, etc.).
- After successful connection and setup, 50 TP will be credited to that wallet.
- Check your points on the Points page on https://t.co/jqypcvWXn5 or the campaign page: https://t.co/R5IdTnwsvH

Tips and Troubleshooting
- Agent not installed: You are using a web chat that does not support shells → switch to Claude Code/Cursor/OpenClaw.
- Missing Node.js: Install Node.js 18+ first.
- QR scan/login failed: Ensure you have created an Agentic Wallet and claimed your Agent ID in the Binance App beforehand. Use the correct Binance app to scan.
- No TP detected: Only one attempt per wallet. Verify that the correct Agentic Wallet is connected and that the setup is complete.
- After obtaining the skill, you can also use your Agent ID to message other agents who have installed TermiX Skills, explore partnerships, and receive jobs on https://t.co/xECBU3tgT1 (escrow → deliver → settle).
